name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Perched at about 3,000 m overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it houses a large Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and is a major Gelugpa center of Tibetan Buddhism.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama nearby

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang on NH-13, surrounded by snow-capped peaks, with nearby Sela Lake (Paradise Lake) that often freezes in winter. Strategic and scenic route.
facts: Connects Tawang to Dirang and rest of India
On NH-13, about 78 km from Tawang
Sela Tunnel provides all-weather access below the pass

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m on the road to Bum La Pass, formed by an earthquake that submerged a forest, leaving dead tree trunks standing in the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song shoot. Surrounded by peaks and meadows.
facts: About 35 km from Tawang towards Bum La
Popular name from Madhuri Dixit film shoot
Army permit often required for access

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: 100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town, about 40 km from Tawang on the highway. Fed by Nuranang Chu from Sela Pass slopes, with a small hydel plant at the base. Scenic stop en route, also known as Bong Bong Falls.
facts: Near Jang, ~2 km northeast of town
On NH-13 between Sela and Tawang
Named after local legend involving Monpa girl Nura
Song from film Koyla shot nearby

name: Bum La Pass
description: Border pass at about 4,600 m (15,200 ft) between India and China (Tibet), 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and 1962 war site; now a Border Personnel Meeting point. Requires special army and DC permits; dramatic high-altitude landscape.

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic monastery near Tawang town, birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso in 1683. Founded in 1489 by Urgen Sangpo, smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, belonging to Nyingma or related traditions, set amid hills.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: 40-foot-high stupa-style memorial near Tawang town dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features names of martyrs, prayer flags, and daily bugle ceremony; overlooks the valley.

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: Army memorial near Nuranang on the highway to Tawang, honoring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles who held off Chinese forces for 72 hours in 1962 and was awarded Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Includes shrine, bunker exhibits, and canteen.
facts: Honors Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat MVC
About 25-40 km from Tawang near Nuranang
Local Monpa revere him as a deity

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso Lake)
description: Serene high-altitude glacial lake about 16-18 km from Tawang on the Bum La road, at roughly 3,700-3,900 m. Surrounded by rhododendrons and peaks, often frozen in winter; quieter alternative to Madhuri Lake with mirror-like waters.
facts: About 16-18 km from Tawang on Bum La road
Permit for Bum La road required

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main town of Tawang at about 2,700-3,000 m elevation, inhabited by Monpa people. Base for exploring monasteries, passes, and valleys; markets, hotels, and cultural experiences of Tibetan-influenced Himalayan life.
facts: Gateway for Bum La and Sela circuits
